subject.title: enhancement: Optimize voice message processing pipeline for Telegram

question: Should Telegram voice optimization become a broad channel/TTS pipeline redesign now, and what stage-ordering, state-snapshot, delivery, caching, and concurrency contract should it use?
rationale: The source-level problem is real, but the requested fixes cross Telegram ingress serialization, STT preflight, TTS delivery, cache persistence, and session-state semantics, which automation cannot safely choose as a product/API direction.

options.title: Define a staged pipeline contract
options.body: Approve a design that names queued, transcribing, processing, synthesizing, and delivering states, preserves message ordering rules, and sets live benchmark acceptance criteria before implementation.

options.title: Keep only narrow UX fixes active
options.body: Treat the typing-cue and split-delivery issues as the actionable near-term work and leave priority queues, streaming STT, and async TTS deferred.

options.title: Defer pending live measurements
options.body: Require live Telegram/macOS arm64 latency traces before deciding which pipeline stages need redesign.

recommendation.title: Define a staged pipeline contract
recommendation.body: Approve a design that names queued, transcribing, processing, synthesizing, and delivering states, preserves message ordering rules, and sets live benchmark acceptance criteria before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available routing signal spans current TTS history, product-surface decisions, and release/current-main ownership rather than one Telegram-only call site.
